user.title: GL.iNet KVM
user.description: Connect to a GL.iNet Comet KVM on your local network.

data_description.host: The KVM's LAN address. Use the IP address rather than a .local name if you have more than one unit.
data_description.port: 443 unless you have moved the web interface.
data_description.username: The KVM's login. Leave empty if the unit has authentication disabled.
data_description.password: The KVM's password. Leave empty if the unit has authentication disabled.
data_description.verify_ssl: Leave off unless you have installed your own trusted certificate; the KVM ships a self-signed one.

data_description.username: The KVM's login. Leave empty if the unit has authentication disabled.

data_description.verify_ssl: Leave off unless you have installed your own trusted certificate.

streamer_stopped.title: The video streamer on {name} is not running
streamer_stopped.description: The KVM's own video streamer is stopped, so the Screen camera has no picture and the capture sensors are unavailable. On GL.iNet firmware the streamer only runs while the GL.iNet web interface is watching. To keep it running, add `kvmd: {streamer: {forever: true}}` to /etc/kvmd/override.yaml on the unit and restart kvmd. This clears itself once the streamer is running again.

msd_offline.title: Virtual media is offline on {name}
msd_offline.description: The KVM reports its mass-storage gadget as offline, so no image can be attached to the host. GL.iNet firmware 1.10.0 ships the mass-storage functions unlinked from the USB gadget; adding `otg: {devices: {msd: {start_cdrom: true, start_flash: true}}}` to /etc/kvmd/override.yaml and rebooting the unit fixes it. This clears itself once the gadget is online.

keys.name: Keys

power.name: Host power

config_entry_id.name: KVM
